contentFetch.title: Full-Text Fetch Fallback (BYOK)
contentFetch.description: For pages that beat every other extraction tier (active bot-protection challenges), bring your own API key for Jina Reader or Firecrawl Cloud — commercial services that specialize in fetching hard-to-reach pages. Used only as a last resort, after this server's own attempts come up empty. Your API key is encrypted at rest and never shared.

sync.renderSidecarDescription: Optional external service that renders JavaScript-heavy or client-only pages, used as a fallback when in-process fetching returns no content.
sync.renderSidecarHint: POST '{url}' receives '{"url": "…"}' and returns the rendered HTML (as text/html or JSON with an html/content field). Point it at a self-hosted crawl4ai or a lean Playwright service. The page you render is still SSRF-checked; nothing leaves your server beyond this sidecar.
sync.renderSidecarGuideIntro: The sidecar is a small, separate container that renders pages in a real browser. FeedFerret ships a ready-to-run one under docker/render-sidecar.
sync.renderSidecarGuideStep1: Add the service below to your FeedFerret docker-compose.yml so both containers share a network.
sync.renderSidecarGuideStep2: Build and start it with the command below (change SIDECAR_TOKEN to your own secret, or remove it to run without a token).
sync.renderSidecarGuideStep3: Turn on the toggle above, paste the Sidecar URL, and enter the same token if you set one.
sync.renderSidecarGuideStep4: Click Test — a green result means it works. From then on it's used automatically as a fallback for full-text and page→feed when in-process fetching finds nothing.
sync.renderSidecarGuideDocsHint: Full contract, security notes and alternatives (e.g. crawl4ai) are in docs/render-sidecar.md.
sync.rsshubDescription: Optional self-hosted RSSHub instance, used for "Add from platform" — turning a YouTube channel, subreddit, GitHub repo releases, etc. into a real feed.
sync.rsshubHint: Point this at your own self-hosted RSSHub instance (docs.rsshub.app). The access key is RSSHub's own optional `?key=` gate (its ACCESS_KEY setting) — leave it blank if your instance doesn't use one. Once a route is validated it's stored as the feed's plain URL, so this key is visible to whichever user adds a platform feed.
sync.changedetectionDescription: Optional self-hosted changedetection.io instance, used for "Monitor this page" — turns any page (including JS-rendered ones, since changedetection.io does its own browser rendering) into a feed of its changes over time.
sync.changedetectionHint: Two different secrets are required: the API key is under Settings → API in your changedetection.io instance; the RSS access token is a separate value that changedetection.io never shows as a copyable field — click "Test connection" below with the API key filled in and it will be auto-detected and filled in for you. A freshly created watch's feed has no items until changedetection.io has checked the page at least twice, so a new "monitor this page" feed can look empty for a while — this is expected, not an error.

accessibility.title: Accessibility Statement
accessibility.commitment: FeedFerret is committed to making its interface accessible to everyone. Our target is WCAG 2.2 Level AA conformance.

features.title: Features
features.skipLink: Skip link: A "Skip to content" link appears at the top of every page when focused.
features.ariaLandmarks: ARIA landmarks: The sidebar uses role="navigation", the article list and reader use role="region" with descriptive labels.
features.keyboardShortcuts: Keyboard shortcuts: All major actions can be performed via keyboard shortcuts. Press ? to see the full list.
features.keyboardNavigation: Keyboard navigation in article lists: Article cards are focusable and activatable with Enter or Space.
features.liveRegions: Screen reader live regions: Unread article counts and search result counts are announced via aria-live regions.
features.reducedMotion: Reduced motion: All animations respect the prefers-reduced-motion media query.
features.iconLabels: Icon button labels: All icon-only buttons carry an aria-label.
features.semanticStructure: Semantic article structure: Article headers use proper h1, author uses address, dates use time.
features.darkMode: Dark mode: Full dark-mode support via the system preference or the in-app toggle.
features.focusManagement: Focus management: Dialogs trap focus and restore it to the trigger element on close.
features.toggleState: Toggle state: Toggle buttons use aria-pressed to communicate state to assistive technologies.

knownLimitations.title: Known Limitations
knownLimitations.dragDrop: Drag-and-drop feed reordering provides keyboard sensors but screen-reader announcements during drag operations have not been fully validated.
knownLimitations.contrast: Contrast for some muted-foreground decorative text elements may fall below 4.5:1 at certain accent color configurations.
knownLimitations.zoom: The 200%-zoom layout has not been formally audited on all screen combinations.
knownLimitations.i18n: The application is available in English and German. Further languages can be contributed via the translation files.

apiPassword.title: API password
apiPassword.description: Use a separate password for Google Reader and Fever clients. Two-factor accounts require it. Without an API password or two-factor authentication, your login password works unless you require an API password. Rotating, revoking, or changing this policy disconnects Google Reader clients. Revoking keeps API passwords required. When an API password exists, the login password never works for API access. Changing your login password keeps the API password and revokes issued GReader tokens.
